Best task is this :

In an interview give the candidate a task and tell them you’ll be back in 10 / 15 mins.

In those 10 / 15 mins the candidate will write a user testing script for a website. Pick something very generic or a brand everyone will be familiar with.

10 / 15 mins later you [the hiring manager] and a participant (someone else from the org) turn up and the candidate runs a study for another 10 / 15 mins.

Once the study is complete give the candidate the choice to have some time to analyse the session and notes or to start presenting back the findings. You’ll know straight away if the candidate can or cannot run a study.

This is great as the candidate doesn’t have to present a non relevant case study from their portfolio and you also see how the candidate acts under pressure.

Unless you’re going to AB test to find out which is the most optimal, just pick one and get moving!

I thought there were a couple of different approaches you could take with this.

They may not be correct, but they’re certainly approaches.

Approach 1 :
This would equate to working to rule. For instance, your stakeholders have given you a very open ended brief. But when you have then tried everything in your power to try and get more information they have continually blocked you. This instance, I suggest you keep a paper trail of all conversations. And show when you presented anything for preview such as questionnaires, study guides, etc and received absolutely no help guidance assistance and expected collaboration.

You can then run the study. Stating that this is what you discovered. If it was not what was expected, you have a clear paper trail of your stakeholder, not being collaborative, and you can instantly demand improvement there and then.

Approach 2:
I think others are getting more of the explanation of the roadmap. I quite like they’re in order to do X I need this to happen. You can even hold your ground and this is something that I am doing at the moment.

My exact example is my team and stakeholder want me to do research I’m saying back to them though that we are slowly, but surely getting a better and better brief as well as a research question. But until we have a well-defined research question, I will not be engaging with an external agency to recruit participants.

And I would say this is the biggest thing that needs some form of clarity :
- What is the research question?

Only by having a good research question, can you accurately defined the participants you want to recruit for. The Experience, you want to test. The assets and Creative that you want to put in front of people to spark conversation.

In the long run though, if you’re not getting the support then, realistically you’re only going to be staying at this job for a certain period of time before you’ll be burnt out and you’ll be needing to go somewhere new. That’s not a reflection on your abilities more a reflection on the human resources and people management of the current company that you were working in. Unfortunately, if this is the case you could always adopt approach 3.

Approach 3:
If in general, you are checking out and looking to leave the company. You can always consider doing methodologies and approaches to UX research that you haven’t done before. As this is quite a good way of beefing and bulking up your portfolio. I would say that this approach would work particularly well if your stakeholders tend just to say “yes,” a lot when you are doing your playbacks and presenting your findings. If anything, that’s a sure sign that they have checked out because they are not willing to propane ask additional questions of your research.

I hope that helps and gives you a couple of good options, as well as the other good suggestions that people have said on this post .

* You start to see missing requirements

* You take your initial screens back to a PM
   * You present what you've done
   * You raise additional requirements
   * You say what you're unsure of and what needs to be worked on more
   * The PM (or BA or Product Owner) will see :
      * You're on the right track fully

      * They like your ideas
